question: Should OpenClaw publish a stable machine-readable Gateway API schema, and if so should it be OpenAPI-shaped, Gateway-protocol-specific, or limited to the existing HTTP compatibility endpoints?
rationale: The current Gateway surface is a mixed WebSocket RPC/event protocol plus selected HTTP endpoints, so exposing a schema would become a public API and security contract rather than a mechanical route dump.

options.title: Design Gateway schema contract
options.body: Publish a scoped, versioned schema/discovery artifact for Gateway methods, events, and HTTP endpoints after deciding auth, scope, and compatibility guarantees.

options.title: Limit to HTTP endpoints
options.body: Only document/generate schema for the OpenAI-compatible HTTP and tools-invoke endpoints, leaving WebSocket RPC client generation out of scope.

options.title: Decline core schema for now
options.body: Keep the existing docs and discovery lists as the supported integration path until maintainers want to freeze a broader client contract.

recommendation.title: Design Gateway schema contract
recommendation.body: Publish a scoped, versioned schema/discovery artifact for Gateway methods, events, and HTTP endpoints after deciding auth, scope, and compatibility guarantees.

likelyOwner.reason: Josh Avant is explicitly listed for Gateway and Security, and this decision crosses both API contract and operator-surface exposure.
